responses.response: REFUSE: The claim's "acceptable performance overhead" is tied to specific tool performance (ollama ~50ms/chunk), which is version-dependent and could change significantly across ollama, python, or bash versions.

Character-based chunking with turn-boundary preservation and multi-layer redaction is a version-independent architectural technique that works regardless of which version of historian or any other tool implements it.

The race condition of concurrent read-decide-write creating duplicates without full-cycle locking is inherent to file-based concurrency and exists in all versions of bash, making the lesson version-independent.
The concurrent write problem exists in any version of bats; run IDs and completion sentinels prevent it as a version-independent mechanism.

Keeping a rolling baseline synchronized with file edits so that subsequent operations don't compare against stale state is a version-independent principle that applies whenever the baseline mechanism exists.

REFUSE: Claim asserts one specific remedy (librarian_lesson_write_atomic) is required when other standard atomic-write patterns (temp file with mv, flock, etc.) also prevent zero-byte files on interruption.
This is a version-independent error-handling principle about warning on stderr after irreversible operations, regardless of how librarian implements the declined-ledger write.
Explicit, unambiguous instructions to an LLM remain more reliably interpreted than vague shorthand across any version of any tool.
REFUSE: The claim depends on ZLesson's schema permanently lacking an artifact_id field, which is a version-specific implementation detail that could change in future versions of librarian.
Tests named for multi-step user stories must implement those exact sequences; simpler variants that pass do not validate the mechanisms are required.
This lesson holds regardless of version: XDG_CONFIG_HOME persistence across HOME reassignment and git's respect for GIT_CONFIG_* environment variable overrides are stable Unix and git mechanisms.

The -r and -c flags are core stable jq features that produce the documented behavior regardless of version; the lesson correctly identifies that -c ensures single-line-per-object output where -r alone does not.

The implementation demonstrates that a scanner built by replicating an existing file-matching pattern handles all required cases—pattern correctness, zero-match reporting, untracked-file exclusion, and non-repo safety—without relying on version-specific bash or git behavior.
GITHUB_TOKEN with id-token:write is a stable OIDC authentication mechanism in GitHub Actions that has been available independently of version and works with all modern git versions.

REFUSE: The claim asserts "acceptable performance overhead," but the evidence provides ollama-specific performance characteristics (~50ms/chunk, <3s total) from a particular version, and different versions could have substantially different performance profiles that might not meet that threshold.

Character-based chunking with turn boundaries and layered redaction is a design pattern that achieves safe idempotency independent of how any tool implements it; the evidence demonstrates historian's successful implementation of this approach, which generalizes beyond historian's version.

Race conditions in concurrent read-decide-write operations and their solution through full-cycle locking with atomic writes via temp-file-plus-rename are fundamental OS principles independent of bash version.
Concurrent writes to a shared file produce ambiguous records regardless of bats version; the fix addresses the underlying I/O contention pattern, not framework behavior.
Keeping tracked state synchronized with actual changes is a version-independent coordination principle that prevents false duplicates regardless of lineage implementation.
REFUSE - the claim mandates a specific function instead of stating the atomic-write principle it solves, creating potential version-dependence on librarian's implementation.
Distinguishing error types and warning on stderr during audit failures after irreversible operations is a version-independent error-handling principle applicable across all librarian versions.
Explicit instructions produce consistent LLM behavior independent of tribunal's version.

REFUSE: The claim depends on ZLesson lacking artifact_id, which is a version-dependent property of the librarian data model that could change in future versions, making the unreachable-branch claim false.

Tests must validate what their names promise; discovering this via snapshot restoration mechanics in librarian doesn't make the principle version-dependent—test design integrity holds regardless of what mechanisms enable the user story.

Unsetting environment variables and redirecting config paths to /dev/null are standard git isolation techniques that work independent of git or bats version, and the evidence correctly identifies why XDG_CONFIG_HOME persistence causes test leakage and how the remedy prevents it.
The need for jq's -c flag to produce JSONL-compatible output is a fundamental property of how jq works, independent of version.
Bash patterns for file matching, repository detection, and standard shell conditionals have remained stable across versions, making this implementation technique version-independent.
GITHUB_TOKEN with id-token:write provides OIDC-based authentication that is stable across git versions and GitHub Actions platforms without requiring manual git credential configuration.

REFUSE: The claim's assertion of "acceptable performance overhead" depends on ollama version performance characteristics—50ms/chunk and <3s overhead specifics that change with different ollama versions would alter whether the overhead remains acceptable.

Character-based chunking with turn-boundary preservation and multi-layer redaction is a general architectural principle for safe, idempotent transcript indexing that holds independent of historian version.
The claim is true regardless of bash version; read-decide-write race conditions and their file-locking solution are fundamental concurrency patterns independent of tooling versions.
Run IDs and completion sentinels are a version-independent pattern for disambiguating concurrent emissions to a shared log, regardless of how bats implements test execution.

The claim describes a fundamental principle of change tracking—that a baseline must be updated whenever the actual file state changes—which holds true regardless of how the lineage or Bash implementations change.

Atomic writes prevent zero-byte files on interrupt the same way across all bash and librarian versions, making this lesson version-independent and consistent with the established pattern already in three other librarian modules.
The principle of distinguishing error types and warning on stderr after an irreversible operation while preserving exit code semantics is version-independent error-handling design.
Explicit instruction structure prevents LLM interpretation drift across all versions.
REFUSE: The claim depends on ZLesson's current schema (lacking artifact_id), which is version-dependent and could change in future librarian releases, making the documented unreachability false.
Tests must implement the sequences their names claim to test, because simpler variants can pass without exercising the intended mechanisms.
The isolation mechanism is based on stable git environment variable handling (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM) and shell behavior that work unchanged across any reasonable git or bats version.

jq's -c and -r flags controlling output format and string encoding have been stable core behavior since jq 1.3, making the claim that -rc ensures compact one-line-per-object output universally true across all supported jq versions.

Mirroring existing matcher logic to build a file scanner is a version-independent approach that depends only on bash's stable core features, validated by test coverage of pattern matching, zero-matches, untracked-file handling, and non-repo safety.
REFUSE: This claim depends on GitHub Actions supporting OIDC token generation, which was introduced in late 2021 and would not hold for earlier runner versions.
